This enables the collection of extensive semantic representations, even for underrepresented acronyms. Evaluating our method with both automatic and human-assisted assessments, we find it effectively disambiguates acronyms within new sets of sentences from the Legal domain and generalizes well to other domains like Biology and Computer Science. Additionally, we develop a simple prototype that integrates our word embeddings into a legal search engine to improve relevant results for users searching by acronyms.

Quantum Hall systems exhibit inherent thelanity due to their edge currents. In contrast to thermal conductance's symmetry under the reversal of magnetic field, its rate of rectification is inherently designed to be straight-forward. In this study, we show that thermal rectification can be successfully achieved through the creation of asymmetrically width-tapered quantum wires in Helium atoms. The theoretical model suggests nearly 100% thermal rectification at low temperature when a sufficient voltage bias is applied. Additionally, we observe that thermal conductance in this setup can be effectively controlled through voltage, leading to an innovative mechanism for thermal regulation in quantum Hall setup.

For large-scale DNA sequencing data analysis, leveraging the index marking system of the Illumina sequencing cluster generation process, we present a highly scalable method for data storage and retrieval. By dividing the data into storage partitions, we efficiently access them using the built-in indexing infrastructure of the Illumina clustering process, thus minimizing the need for additional tags. We demonstrate how our scheme can be further optimized by using the full spectral capabilities of the Illumina reading process and present a comprehensive simulation and theoretical assessment of this partition management strategy. Additionally, we discuss the incorporation of error-correcting codes to guarantee data integrity.

This study examines numerical results for nodal lines in the momentum space of three-dimensional time-reversal invariant topological insulators with sparse disorder. These particular topological charge distributions are found in classes AII and AIIU(1). Both the random spin-flip mechanism, which models weak disorder in spin strength, and the strong disorder in neighbor distance between atoms are explored. Both methods preserve time-reversal symmetry but not translational symmetry. We analyze the spatial distribution of nodal lines following their transition into the insulating phase, with results indicating that the disorder-induced randomness in topological charge leads to the formation of irregular, clumped N-dimensional surfaces in d-dimensional space. In the case of weak disorder, the charge is distributed uniformly, but in disorder-regime, the charge clusters and clumps merge. These findings confirm the stability of nodal lines and provide insight into the natural occurrence of topological nodes in nature.

This work explores the concept of waves emanating from a single oscillator and the influence of connecting multiple oscillators, whose movements are linked by springs. The research finds that the connection between adjacent frequency and wave speed is influenced by the connection's stiffness, spatial alignment of the secondary oscillator, and the direction in which it affects the primary oscillator. Notably, the connection between adjacent stiffness and wave speed is not universally positive, yet aligns under specific conditions, particularly when the interaction occurs in a spatially localized manner and influences the primary oscillator in the direction of wave propagation, thus making this correlation positive in such scenarios, as observed in various phenomena like myelinated saltatory conduction, crystal myriapods, and deep-sea communication.

This study introduces an algorithm for approximating entropy estimation that operates efficiently with limited data, and is able to provide accurate results with high confidence. The algorithm only requires input data with entropy values above zero, as it can handle cases with minimal entropy. By contrast, existing methods with similar guarantees are not feasible to implement in practice due to their high data requirements. The proposed algorithm has a time complexity of O(1/p(1-δ)n), where 'n' represents the size of the input data, 'p' is the probability of selecting an element, and 'δ' is a factor controlling the error rate. The algorithm achieves an ε-close result with (1-δ) probability, and it has an ε error that is directly proportional to the square root of the entropy 'H'. The algorithm is implemented empirically, and results show that it provides more accurate entropy estimates with less data than the state-of-the-art methods with the same data complexity.

The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) in medical fields has led to a surge in the gathering of medical data on a large scale, thus necessitating the planning of comprehensive medical data archives, known as imaging biobanks. Imaging biobanks that specialize in neurology, oncology, cardiology and other fields are essential for the development and implementation of AI solutions. This paper describes a innovative approach to creating and operating imaging biobanks through the implementation of cloud-based data storage systems, along with the development of unique methodologies to ensure quality, security and efficient management. We showcase our experience in constructing and deploying cloud-based imaging biobanks that support applications in oncology, neurology and other medical specialities.

Machine learning models for medical diagnosis are becoming increasingly accurate, but their reliance on specific patient features for optimal performance is also their main drawback. To mitigate this issue, several data augmentation methods have been developed to enhance their performance in the presence of extra clinical features. However, it has been observed that data augmentation can also improve the model's predictive capabilities when only typical data is available, but its effectiveness in predicting medical diagnoses has not been fully understood in the context of augmented data. 

This research investigates data augmentation techniques for clinical data with two distinct objectives: (1) to enhance prediction performance with limited data sets and (2) to produce diverse but clinically plausible augmented data sets. To accomplish this, a comparative data augmentation approach is proposed, which takes into consideration clinical similarities and feature relationships to generate slightly modified clinical data sets. 

The proposed method employs two techniques: SuperLearn and CLIP, a Bayesianinduced augmentation approach. Both techniques learn from full-data sets and produce minor variations of individual data points. Additionally, a data visualization approach is proposed, which utilizes Bayesian probabilistic models to visualize augmented data in high-dimensional spaces. 

The proposed approach is evaluated on medical data sets, which demonstrate its robustness in both objectification and subjectification tasks.

We provide a concrete example of a polymatroidal ideal based on a rank function that is non-linear when applied to a linear interpretation of the natural numbers. Furthermore, the paper seeks to identify the geometric properties of polymatroidal varieties, especially those derived from the intersection of a polymatroid with a hyperplane, by initializing them under various weighted degree interpretations. The analysis will reveal how different weightings influence the coordinates of the intersection point.

A proposed quantum algorithm aims to minimize the steps necessary for k-means clustering. The algorithm's quantum approach utilizes the quantum multiplicative update method and the quantum nearest level method, designed for convex optimization problems. By taking advantage of oracles that evaluate functions and their gradients, the method demonstrates a reduced number of quantum operations compared to the standard quantum Harrow-Kalaimai algorithm. The authors also discuss conditions under which the multiplicative update method can be optimized using a level optimization technique. The resulting quantum algorithm demonstrates cloud dependence on input data for the FaceScape dataset and is shown to have superior complexity properties. Specifically, its complexity properties are $O(p^{3/2}\epsilon^{-1}\log(E/\epsilon))$ queries, $O(p\epsilon^{-1}\log(E/\epsilon))$ unit gates, and $O(p\epsilon^{-1}\log(E)\log(E/\epsilon))$ asymptotically, where the parameters represent dimensions of the dataset, desired error tolerance, and data range. Additionally, the proposed method offers improved efficiency and a simpler structure, and is complementary to previous quantum algorithms that use amplitude amplification. The project's code is available for review on the Qiskit GitHub repository.

The HATNet planetary transit survey continues to find new planets, contributing to a more comprehensive understanding of the planet mass ratio function in the current database of 11,000+ confirmed exoplanets. Utilizing a combination of the CHIME algorithm and manual review, researchers identified 544 planetary systems, leading to the confirmation of 63 new planets. These new discoveries, when incorporated into the current dataset, do not significantly alter the planet mass ratio function, particularly for a specific q range of  to 0.03. However, they do shift the upper limit of this range to approximately 0.02. The analysis will be further updated once data from a follow-up campaign using the Magellan, VLT, and LAMOST facilities becomes available.

We introduce a novel technique for calculating shadows that reduces the wasteful ray tracing that occurs for points unaffected by casted shadows. This method optimizes the traditional ray-tracing approach, which can be unnecessary for many points on high-resolution surfaces, by limiting shadow checks to surface points with globally visible geometry. A level-of-detail algorithm determines which points have a chance of being in a shadow, by tracing paths from each point and identifying potential occluders. A hardware-accelerated implementation of this algorithm on FPGAs demonstrates improved performance, achieving a 3000-fold speedup for an average case and a 30-fold speedup when applied to ray-traced global illumination. A software implementation is also included, which provides up to a 1000-fold speedup in average tests and up to a 30-fold speedup in rendering intricate scenes with numerous occluders.

The estimation of the spatially distributed O-D demand matrix from link flow observations remains a longstanding challenge in probabilistic O-D demand modeling. This paper proposes a novel estimation framework based on a probabilistic gravity model combined with convex optimization. By invoking Jensen's inequality, we transform the original non-convex estimation problem into a convex optimization problem with an adjustable lower bound. This new formulation enables the application of efficient algorithms and a wide range of existing algorithms can be utilized. The application of Lasso regularization further refines the estimation of the covariance matrix, leading to improved convergence rates and enhanced performance. Our approach is supported by theoretical guarantees and empirical results, demonstrating its ability to provide reliable O-D demand estimates and accurately recover the covariance matrix. The approach also exhibits superior generalization ability and robustness to noise compared to existing methods.

This work investigates the stability of phase-locked states in a pair of oscillators subjected to coupling. Initially, we consider the case of purely linear frequency dispersion, demonstrating both necessary and sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability of the phase-locked state. We then expand the analysis to incorporate weak nonlinear frequency damping, which affects the time-domain asymptotic stability. In this scenario, we both derive conditions for stability and identify how it influences the large time behavior of perturbed phase-locked states. These conditions also determine the shape of periodic solutions emerging from phase-locked states due to time-resonance. We ultimately consider even a strong nonlinear frequency damping regime, finding that perturbed phase-locked states can both attract and repel depending on parameters, thus defying any general frequency dispersion-based stability criteria.

Two prominent mountain car simulation algorithms, the First Best Search (FBS) and the Updated First Best Search (UFS), have proven effective in their fields. We have updated these algorithms to create a uniform method for generating the uniform spanning tree of a directed graph. The updated approach significantly speeds up computations by a factor proportional to the graph's number of vertices, $O(n)$, when used in repeated applications. The method combines the advantages of Wilson's algorithm and the random orientation technique. The uniform spanning tree generation for a given vertex's shortest path tree can also be accelerated by a parameter-hased search within O($n$) time. The techniques are illustrated with actual applications.

We introduce MusicTM-Dataset, a comprehensive music library that links audio recordings with metadata, including lyrics, to facilitate learning unified music representations across multiple modalities. The dataset encompasses 12,000 songs from six music genres, each labeled with text data and inverted pitch contours, and is supplemented with an extensive collection of descriptions to support cross-modal retrieval tasks. We explore a novel approach to this problem by leveraging the musical structure of segments and showing that music representation learning can be enhanced through self-supervised tasks. The results of our experiments with the dataset are made publicly available to inspire further research in this area.

Ontodia is a visual data exploration tool that helps users navigate datasets like Wikidata and other RDF datasets using a unified and intuitive interface. It enhances user experience by allowing users to build queries with a queries builder and dynamically explore data properties with dynamic filters. On top of this, users can customize their exploration by saving configurations or applying pre-built visual templates. We tested Ontodia's effectiveness in exploring Wikidata with a comparison of user sessions and found that it meets our initial expectations and provides a consistent view of the data.

In a trapped one-dimensional Bose-Einstein condensate described by the Gross-Pitaevskii energy, we investigate the traveling solitons that arise as critical points under a specific constraint on the H^1-norm and velocity. We demonstrate that almost all traveling solitons with non-zero velocity are unstable in this constrained environment, but those near the orbital stability threshold for a particular soliton are unstable. We identify the traveling solitons that may be stable, however, and find them to be the locally asymptotically stable dark solitons that occur when the trapping potential is balanced by an external force.

OurLotse is an open-source Python package for cosmology, built on top of Boltzmann solvers such as CodeForCosmo. It enables the efficient implementation of various cosmology analyses through its Lotse module, which offers guidance strategies to automate complex computations. These strategies can be integrated into workflows or used as reusable functions, facilitating rapid development of new analyses and experiments. To streamline the setup of customization options, OurLotse includes the Lotse Parameter class for defining essential parameters such as initial power spectrum parameters and MCMC boundaries. Ourlotse's functionality is showcased through practical examples demonstrating the efficient execution of standard and advanced cosmology analyses. Ourlotse's comprehensive documentation is available at https://ourlotse.readthedocs.io, supplemented by in-depth example tutorials at https://ourlotse.readthedocs.io/en/latest/experimental/.

Achieving a stable, high-beta, nested flux surface configuration in the L-Mode LHD requires careful management of control coils and island control techniques. The optimal coil placement for this purpose was investigated through the use of an optimization algorithm and confirmatory experimental results. By positioning control coils at strategic locations, particularly between the vertical edge and the bottom edge, the control of nested flux surfaces' flexibility and volume is significantly enhanced. Additionally, the technique of resonant magnetic oscillation (RMO) driving of X-point reconnection is found to efficiently generate the high-β L-Mode LHD X-point configuration. RMO-driven reconnection results in a comparable or slightly reduced maximum β_𝑞=0 and three distinct flux surface states, showcasing the potential of this technique in future devices.

A nonintrusive proton resonance frequency shift (PRFS) technique is under development for measuring the temperature of fluids inside reactors. Future reactors will utilize high-practical yield superconducting solenoid magnets to generate large main magnetic fields, enabling a temperature-based proton resonance frequency shift measurement that could be implemented as a distributed temperature sensor. This work aims to investigate the temperature dependence of the proton resonance frequency in high-practical yield yield magnetic fields relevant to future reactors, while assessing the potential of PRFS as a reactor diagnostic tool. A 211-MWe, 12-tesla experiment and a 500-MWe, 15-tesla reactor were studied, with results showing a nonintrusive temperature measurement range of ~50 mK and a potential for simultaneous temperature profiling across a reactor's volume.

While experiments in the B21 collaboration have demonstrated that multiple distinct condensates in spinor fermion mixtures can be achieved, a theoretical understanding of this phenomenon in certain two-species mixtures has not been fully developed. We propose a new theoretical framework, multicomponent mean-field theory (MCMT), which effectively describes forms of multiple distinct condensates in two-species fermion mixtures. We find that in a two-species mixture, only one type of distinct condensate can be formed, but in a three-species mixture, up to three types of distinct condensates can be formed. We also identify specific parameters for two- and three-species mixtures that can be adapted to the parameters in B21 to verify our findings. Notably, our research reveals a form of distinct condensate not yet observed in B21, which can be formed by adjusting the interaction strengths in a two-species mixture to be zero or non-zero.

Solar flares release energy rapidly, generating magnetic disturbances that speed along a particular path over a specific set of sunspots.  This study investigates whether these disturbances move at the same speed, independent of their varying intensities.  To gather data, researchers used the SDO/AIA satellite to observe a solar flare on March 9, 2023, while a specific coronal hole provided context for the observations.  This study found that the disturbances moved at speeds ranging from 45 to 120 kilometers per second, with more intense disturbances moving at slower speeds.  Researchers observed the disturbances increasing in speed and size before decreasing in a specific area near the center of active region 3664.  This suggests a relationship between the disturbances' behavior and the solar flare event's impact.

A new, simplified proof of the Madsen-Weiss theorem is provided, combining elements of the b-principle and a generalised stability result. This involves understanding the structure of the Madsen-Weiss space using the last mod $p$ Steenrod operation and generalised Morava $E$-theory. Ultimately, the proof relies on the strong rationalisation of the mod $p$ Kurepa number.

This paper provides an explicit performance dependency on key parameters for the BDDC method when used to solve nonlinear problems with Bregman iteration. By combining previous findings, it derives a complex but precise formula for how the BDDC method's convergence is influenced by various parameters. Furthermore, the paper offers practical recommendations for reducing the impact of these parameters. Its theoretical framework is then applied to specific nonlinear problems, such as Roberts' problem, while acknowledging some limitations in the current analysis. Finally, the paper highlights potential areas for future research and uses numerical tests to validate its findings.

The success of Web 2.0 systems heavily relies on user-created metadata, which helps both humans and machines to organize, retrieve, and analyze large amounts of data. To understand user behavior while creating tags, researchers studied 3,131 users over two years across four widely-used tagging services. By understanding how users use tags, we can improve the methods people use to tag and design new, more efficient tagging methods. Our research focuses on one broadening, then narrowing down to specific patterns of tag usage, including 19 different discovery strategies. By analyzing these patterns, we can design new, effective tagging methods and improve existing ones by suggesting user behaviors that aren't always effective.

To develop efficient microscopic acoustic metamaterials, precise design is essential due to non-trivial thermal and viscous interactions at small scales. In this study, we analyze the influence of these interactions on a microscopic resonator acoustical transformer, recently demonstrated by Zhang et al., and investigate how to achieve complete conversion and efficient transmission of acoustic energy. By applying a scattering matrix framework, we determine the metabolic cost and optimize the metabolic efficiency of the device. Our theoretical findings are verified through numerical simulations and a simple physical model. Ultimately, our research provides a clear picture of how to achieve optimal acoustic transmission in microscopic devices by minimizing the metabolic energy invested.

This research focuses on solving the FENE dumbbell model, where we've demonstrated the existence of a unique global weak solution within a specific context of low-frequency conditions in certain function spaces. Additionally, we've showed that under the assumption of small initial values, the model has a singular property where any initial condition leads to a solution that eventually stabilizes over time. This study builds on prior work by Giga and Miyakawa for the Navier-Stokes equations, but we've also addressed conditions under which the solution will remain small, including cases of small data and norm of the solution.

MyBazaar, a novel marketplace application, synchronized the movement of user groups with mobile IAB base stations to ensure continuous connectivity during their real-time exploration of a city. These base stations moved with the leading group, while the remaining groups received data via a network of relays. Researchers examined different non-ideal channel conditions and evaluated two methods for managing the leading group's data - either using a queue-based system or an immediate transmission with real-time service. Both were compared with a reference where all groups moved in unison. Results showed that the queue-based method, despite being designed to support group mobility, experienced data losses, and these losses were greater than the sum of the losses from individual users, due to its sensitivity to the movement of the leading group. In contrast, the transmission with real-time service, although more complex, achieved the same level of efficiency as if the data were being sent to a stationary base station, and this efficiency was also higher than the efficiency of users in unison. Furthermore, the study found that the theoretical model's loss estimates were more accurate when using real data and were conservative in nature.

The effectiveness of machine learning algorithms is highly sensitive to changes in performance when hyperparameters are altered. In this research, an investigation is conducted to determine if modifications in the hyperparameters of one algorithm influence the optimal settings of its peers. We collect an extensive dataset of hyperparameters and associated performance results for multiple machine learning algorithms, and conduct a statistical analysis. We also develop and test a simulation to model the relationships (correlations) between hyperparameters across the different algorithms. Our findings reveal significant interactions between hyperparameters of the various machine learning algorithms, supporting the notion that these settings are interdependent and can be utilized to optimize the overall performance of the algorithms.

In this project, we trace the quantization of energy levels in the electromagnetic field, following the path laid out in Paul Dirac's first quantum electrodynamics paper, emphasizing how it connects to the historically significant Balmer series.

Reinforcement learning makes significant contributions to this field. However, the literature is vast and the diversity of studied tasks is limited, hindering a comprehensive understanding and comparison of the gathered knowledge. This paper introduces the RL-Graph, a hierarchical curriculum of 12 levels, 106 levels, and 215 tasks, spanning from basic to complex tasks in both continuous and discrete control settings. The RL-Graph offers a comprehensive framework for comparing and understanding the impact of recent changes in the reinforcement learning field through extensive experiments with the latest and past state-of-the-art algorithms. The results of these experiments are displayed RL-Graph and the associated analysis are displayed https://www.reinforcement-learning-graph.com.

Liger is a comprehensive software framework for stream processing that runs on a single GPU through parallel execution of stream processing circuits. The framework consists of a stream processing language interpreter, a circuit compiler, and an execution engine. The compiler translates a coded circuit and its input data into a functional unit by the execution engine, which is then paralledy executed on a GPU. The execution engine includes four key components: the kernel generator, kernel memory manager, stream processing kernel, and circular offset table. The stream processing kernel is efficiently executed by leveraging the registor file, shared memory, and global memory of the GPU.

Building upon the recent findings of Alazzam, Tadmor, and Vasseur, our research explores nontrivial traveling waves that arise near the Couette flow with a very small Reynolds number ($R\ll 1$) and significant transverse velocity ($u_2 = O(1)$). The new study demonstrates the existence of such traveling waves under a crucial condition where the waves' speed is significantly slower than a critical threshold determined by the domain's periodic length and the Reynolds number. Through the application of the 'energy method,' we prove local stability for these waves when they are close to the base flow with a high level of smoothness. Notably, the resulting stability criterion matches the known behavior for the standard Reynolds number, highlighting an important distinction in the influence of the Reynolds number on nontrivial vs. trivial traveling waves. Furthermore, our analysis can be extended to other flow patterns such as the Taylor-Gouy flow, which is characterized by the interaction of multiple velocities in the flow.

The way light is polarized is crucial in many areas, like spintronics, nonlinear optics and data-carrying light communications. By better controlling how light is polarized, we can have a bigger impact on these fields. To control light polarization on a global scale, we're developing special photonic structures that can interact with light across wide areas, fields, and frequencies. Since different parts of light are orthogonal to each other, our photonic structures that control polarization also use this concept by combining various light properties. For example, we're developing T-junctions that can guide light from separate waveguides with different phases, creating a phase shift. By adding lateral stress during fabrication, we're developing a global control method that can change light phase across an entire chip. We're also discovering new ways to control light using angular momentum, where we've developed special photonic structures that can transfer the angular momentum of circularly polarized light to trapped light, giving it a helical phase. This allows us to create isolated "island islands" and "toroid cavities" that can confine light in complex ways, opening up opportunities for studying light-matter interactions.

This study provides an integral expression for a solution to a specific equation that can be connected to the solution of a stochastic partial differential equation known as the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation on a bounded area. We show that this solution can be expanded into a infinite series of a special type of function. By applying a result derived from this series, we prove the existence of a solution for values of a given parameter less than zero, but demonstrate that a solution does not exist when that parameter is greater than or equal to zero. Moreover, our findings are valid within the context of a more general scenario that involves a stochastic process in a higher-dimensional space.

This study examines the challenges of using public data in South Africa to monitor and manage the COVID-19 pandemic. It highlights data-related obstacles that impede effective decision-making, including inconsistencies in formatting, missing values, and difficulties in accessing real-time information. The aim is to stimulate a discussion among stakeholders on addressing these issues to ensure effective epidemic response. Moreover, the paper explores the implications of utilizing data for public health. It suggests that an individual's data contribution should be acknowledged. A practical approach to this concept is developed to quantify the individual impact on data-driven decisions. The paper also investigates current methods that consider individual data in decision-making processes and discusses their limitations. A new method is proposed to address these issues, allowing for more precise decision-making by incorporating individual data in the calculation of data-driven metrics. The approach is tested using real-time data from the South African government to demonstrate its feasibility.

Allowing a limited number of components in combinations fundamentally alters the characteristics of subsets of integers. In this research, we investigate the changes in properties when a bounded number of components are permitted in combinations, such as summands in sums, terms in sequences, or factors in products. We demonstrate two key results: (1) In combinations with a bounded number of components, subsets of integers still exhibit the guaranteed presence of arithmetic progressions but lack the guaranteed presence of geometric progressions. (2) In combinations with a bounded number of components, subsets of integers can contain geometric progressions but lack the guaranteed presence of arithmetic progressions. These findings highlight the significance of the number of components in combinations and their impact on the structure of subsets of integers.

We introduce Hierarchical Fusion (Hi-Fusion), a new method for multi-modal 3D object detection that overcomes limitations in current early and intermediate fusion approaches. Instead, Hi-Fusion systematically integrates information from multiple sources in a sequential manner, ultimately yielding a unified output. The method's effectiveness is demonstrated on LIDAR-Fusion with the nuScenes dataset, outperforming other fusion methods by a significant margin, with an mAP improvement of 2.76. We also confirm its versatility and effectiveness in other combinations of modalities and frameworks.

The COVID-19 pandemic has brought an unmatched level of urgency to the task of predicting patient survival rates, given the challenge it poses to the global health care system. With numerous variants spreading rapidly, maintaining essential health care services has become even more difficult, emphasizing the need for an efficient triage system to save lives. This study focuses on specific features that can be extracted from patient data, excluding sensitive personal information, which may serve as valuable non-invasive indicators for patient outcomes. By focusing on characteristics like oxygen saturation levels, heart rate, temperature, and blood pressure, a neural network model is proposed. This model can be trained on publicly available datasets, such as the MIMIC-III, while adhering to privacy constraints. By analyzing migration patterns of COVID-19, this research aims to identify at-risk regions and allocate medical resources effectively through a case study.

We investigate the transmission eigenvalue problem for second-order elliptic differential equations in N-dimensional space. In this space, we consider inhomogeneous media defined by transmission functions $\gamma (x)$ and $\beta (x)$. These functions are built from real-valued components $a, b, c, d$ and constant values. Notably, we focus on the scenario where all inhomogeneous media parameters are real and the transmission eigenfunctions associated with the transmission eigenvalues lie within the set of solutions to the transmission eigenvalue problem.

The set of solutions to the transmission eigenvalue problem is an infinite-dimensional vector space, in which the eigenfunctions related to the non-zero transmission eigenvalues are the orthogonal ones. The associated eigenfunctions exhibit different behaviors based on the medium's parameters: they display perfect localization around the boundary of the ball in N-dimensional space when the medium's parameters are constant, and they display partial localization when the parameters vary with location. The transmission eigenfunctions also demonstrate the ability to reconstruct the potential inside the N-dimensional ball through an increasing sequence. The present research serves as an introduction to a more detailed study on our model's theoretical framework.

This paper presents a novel text generation model that leverages pre-training on a diverse set of text tasks to learn robust utterance representations. By combining various text classification tasks across benchmarks, our model is able to learn robust representations that perform well on challenging text generation tasks. Specifically, we evaluate our model on two text generation tasks: text summarization and text paraphrasing, and observe that strategies involving balanced and weighted loss functions can significantly improve its performance. Notably, the enhanced utterance representations produced by our model transfer effectively to related tasks, such as sentiment analysis and named entity recognition. Additionally, we develop a novel sampling method that allows for more efficient training of text generation models by leveraging a larger corpus without increasing computational costs.

The universal bundle functor, denoted as $G$, transforms the category of simplicial groups to itself. Researchers have long regarded $G$ as a monad within the category of simplicial groups. This paper verifies the monadicity conditions for $G$ as previously proposed by Barr and Wells. The study begins by demonstrating that $G$ induces a monad on the category of simplicial pairs. Furthermore, the paper establishes the full monad structure on this category, including a comonad on the category of simplicial groups, whose interaction with the monad structure of $G$ within this category is examined.

For any finite abelian group G, let's denoted the number of its subgroups by $r_G$, with $r_1$ representing the total number of subgroups. Through investigation, it is found that the value of $r_{G_1 \times G_2}$ is equal to the product of the number of subgroups of $G_1$ and the number of subgroups of $G_2$. Additionally, it is demonstrated that the number of subgroups of a finite abelian group is an anisotropic anisotropic function of its order, with the number of subgroups of a finite abelian group of order $n$ being $O(n^{1/2} \log (n))$. Finally, it is established that the number of subgroups of a finite abelian group of order $n$ is $O_{{\varepsilon}}(n^{1/2+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$.

We begin with the Hertzian non-linear $S^{(1,0)}$ element model, a discrete in space and time system where we obtain the Korteweg-de Vries equation in the continuum, with a particular limit being the Galilean invariant Stokes wave. Utilizing a singular gauge transformation, we develop a Hamiltonian formulation for the system, which shows that in the Hamiltonian Pelcovits-Schrieffer limit, it has a canonical structure, thus being integrable at a particular level of symmetry. We utilize the Lagrangian formulation to directly demonstrate invariance under Bäcklund transformations, which, when combined with the Kelvin reflection symmetry, leads to a Darboux transformation solution method. This allows us to derive a Bäcklund equation and generate non-trivial soliton solutions in general initial conditions.

The task of Visual Relationship Detection involves the challenging identification of object-to-object semantic relationships in images, but current research is limited by suboptimal negative sampling methods. We introduce BNPS, a balanced sampling strategy that mitigates network bias and enhances detection performance. BNPS dynamically constructs proposal images based on the current classification margins, and its weighting is weighted by class frequency to achieve frequency balance. We further refine BNPS by creating a bounding box generator that generates targeted, difficult samples for optimization. Experiments on the VR-50K and VRAO datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of BNPS, yielding SOTA results and nearly perfect binary classification accuracy (0.998) on the VRAO dataset.

A strategy is proposed to extract any form of quantum behavior from a system subjected to a strong decoherence process. In this context, the scenario of a bit-flip channel is considered, and it is demonstrated that any remnant of quantum behavior within a shared state can be externally taken out via a strong measurement. The remaining state within the system effectively becomes classical. Two forms of quantum behavior are explored in this process - the Heisenberg uncertainty relation and entanglement. While partial extraction in both cases is achievable for strong measurement outcomes close to a specific value, only a strong measurement near its maximum value leads to significant extraction in both scenarios. Two methods of calculating extraction efficiency are also considered, yielding similar results for one, but a significant discrepancy in the other. Finally, it is noted that the efficiency of extraction is not a fixed property but is instead a function of the specific channel parameter involved.

Researchers have developed Gated Recurrent Units to successfully track an individual's changing characteristics over time, but their application in social networks to update a person's relationship with another over time is less explored. In this research, we present a novel social network analysis framework, which combines a graph of interconnected units of analysis with a sequence model of temporal patterns. The graph maintenance module uses a gradient-based approach to update the relationships between units of analysis, while the temporal analysis module is an GRU that predicts and refines the connections. By introducing an attention mechanism to focus the GRU on current and past relevant connections, our framework outperformed several baseline and combination models. Notably, the baseline models consisted of a simple graph, an un gated recurrent unit, and a combination of both. Through comprehensive experiments on multiple social network datasets, our framework consistently demonstrated improved performance. Moreover, the significance of current and past connections was evaluated and found to be crucial in predicting future connections.

In neural network training, constructing complex graph-based models often leads to computationally expensive operations, which can be avoided using adaptive sampling techniques. By dynamically selecting key graph nodes, efficient graph convolution operations can be performed on a reduced dataset, enabling faster model training and inference. However, standard sampling methods may not fully leverage these techniques. By incorporating task-specific information into the sampling process, we propose a novel method that enhances accuracy while significantly reducing computational costs. This method's performance and complexity-reduction capabilities are validated through experiments on various classification and link prediction tasks across multiple networks.

This implementation of the Computer Language (CL) rules is designed to facilitate the creation of high-quality Multiple Constant Multiplication (MCM) circuits. It follows the methodology outlined in the paper of Genoa et al. (Designs. 2019), but focuses on more efficient implementation details. By applying the CL methods for bit-vector representation, bit removal, and error handling, it becomes possible to develop MCM circuits that achieve a balance between circuit size and yield. This approach of error propagation is crucial for realizing the true trade-off between circuit quality and yield.

Recent breakthroughs in quantum computing and machine learning have sparked significant interest in quantum deep learning.  Quantum deep learning has the potential to bridge the fields, but due to a lack of quantum hardware, current research is confined to simulations using NISQ (Noisy Intermediate Scale Quantum) devices.  As a result, there are significant limitations to the performance of quantum deep learning models, making it difficult to evaluate their true potential compared to classical neural networks.  To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes the QSHANN (Quantum Shadow Architecture Network) that leverages quantum computing principles combined with statistical analysis based on Pauli measurements.  By employing hybrid quantum-classical neural networks, we demonstrate that our approach overcomes current quantum deep learning limitations, enabling its independent use.  Extensive numerical experiments were conducted on six public image datasets, and found that our method achieves an 11.4% higher average test accuracy than similar models such as QDCNN and QSNN.  Furthermore, the proposed network also exhibits improved efficiency in terms of time complexity.

The radio frequency (RF) technology developed for high energy physics has remained largely unchanged in other RF applications, but recent advancements in HF accelerators and the reactivation of magnetically confined fusion reactors have created new opportunities for innovation in RF electronics. This article explores the historical context of RF technology and the specific needs of users in HF accelerators and magnetically confined fusion systems, highlighting the differences between their technologies and the potential for collaborative research to meet their requirements in the future.

The High-Luminosity LHC and the new HL-LHC upgrade have made it clear the path for a high-energy muon collider, with an even more compelling argument for its development and operation. This comprehensive overview delves into the comprehensive needs of a high-energy muon collider, including its major design and operational challenges such as the efficient creation, control, and acceleration of muons in the presence of intense magnetic fields and high-rate decays, all while providing a clear rationale for the immense scientific benefits and a knowledge gap in the field of particle physics that only a high-energy muon collider can fill.

We examine the spectrum of long-wavelength fluctuations in relativistic fluids of spin-0 and spin-1 particles, utilizing kinetic theories and effective field theories (EFTs) to establish a generalized, phenomenological framework. This framework includes specific fluid types as special cases. Our analysis of effective actions reveals the universality of certain dispersion patterns regardless of the underlying particle composition, and this finding is verified by comparing with kinetic theories. Furthermore, we develop a simplified model to represent the effective actions of scalar and vector modes, which can be expressed through two characteristic coefficients. This model also extends to gauge theories, where we recalculate the relevant coefficients and validate the predicted dispersion patterns with the original kinetic theory approach.

The calculation of particle radiation from massive black holes formed in collisions between primordial black holes and stars has been performed. It's been found that the Hawking radiation emitted by black holes has a significant impact on the overall flux of low-energy photons, particularly in situations where the mass of the black hole is around 10^15 grams. The black hole merger-induced radiation cannot be ignored when exploring the broader context of primordial black hole evaporation.

Evaluating a logic circuit is a fundamental task in computer science.
Using the BLR algorithm, we can model circuit evaluation as a dynamic process.
We show that a specialized processor with a self-correcting comparison unit is optimal for evaluating such circuits.
By designing a pipeline that matches the circuit's depth, we can achieve a speedup of at least the circuit's depth plus one.
Using this efficient pipeline, we develop an error-finding algorithm and a deterministic algorithm for identifying faulty gates, both of which run in time proportional to the number of evaluated circuit gates plus the square root of that number times the number of errors.
We also demonstrate that, if finding the faults is unnecessary, our error-finding algorithm speed can be reduced by a factor of the square root of the number of errors.

This paper presents an algorithmic solution for efficiently approximating valued constraints in complex problems. Research has previously established a general algorithm that guarantees a constant-time approximation algorithm for valued constraints within specific constraints; this new work expands upon these results by providing an algorithmic solution for minimisation problems with broader constraints. Specifically, the revised algorithm is applicable to valued constraints within the parameters of two variables r and s, which allows the approach to achieve optimal results for specific scenarios such as valued cubic constraints when r equals s. Furthermore, the method is flexible and can be adapted to achieve optimal results for valued n-k constraints when r equals n/2.

Recent studies on few-shot parsing have demonstrated the efficacy of applying few-shot learning principles to improve the performance of parsing methods. However, it has been observed that few-shot parsing methods are highly sensitive to their training and validation sets in few-shot parsing tasks. This paper aims to investigate this issue and reveals that FPIO, a pioneering few-shot parsing method, achieves its best results when trained and evaluated using the same limited annotated data source available for a target language. FIO surpasses other few-shot parsing approaches by a significant margin of 3.1 parse accuracy percentage points under this specific evaluation setting. Moreover, FPIO evaluates its own target language's performance relative to its own target language's performance and outperforms its own parsing methods. FIO's superior performance is further solidified when compared to its own parsing methods. FIO's own parsing methods. FIO's own parsing methods. FIO's own parsing methods. FIO's own parsing methods. FIO's own parsing methods.

In this study, we apply machine learning techniques to the identification of specific materials within hyperspectral images, then modify the resulting labels to enhance semantic segmentation performance without additional input data. By leveraging a horizontal shift and multi-label conversion, we utilize common sense knowledge from human experts and neighboring pixels to redefine each label in the image, then train a segmentation model using only the modified labels as supervision. Through comparative analysis on two datasets, we found that the existing labels have some positive impact on segmentation accuracy, but the processing method we propose provides a substantial improvement with a notable increase in inter-class variability and the precision of class boundaries.

The analysis of data from the Kepler and K2 missions has revealed an unusual pattern in the rotation of a specific star, an old, cool subgiant with a spectral type of G or K. This star, identified as KIC 8967654, exhibits unusually low and variable rotation rates that diverge from commonly observed patterns. Its age, approximately 12 billion years, suggests that it may lie at the endpoint of stellar evolution for stars on the main sequence with a mass similar to the Sun. This case provides an extreme limit on the duration of the main sequence phase for such stars. Moreover, it presents an anomaly that requires explanation, potentially stemming from an irregular distribution of angular momentum among the stars in the dense central region of the globular cluster where it resides, or the result of an interaction between the star and its companion celestial bodies that caused it to adopt an irregular rotation pattern.

This research introduces a modified RAM model for computing positive integers, similar to the standard RAM model used for computing polynomials. A new representation is proposed for integers within the range $2^{poly}$, consisting of at most a quadratic number of 64-bit words. By leveraging this encoding, any polynomial-computation RAM program can be translated into an equivalent universal RAM program in polytime. Furthermore, the research investigates another question related to integer RAM and develops an efficient time-different version of the encoding, consisting of at most $O(\log b)$ words for an integer $b$. Under the assumption that the discrete logarithm problem in multiplicative groups is not in P, this alternative encoding is not translatable like the previous one.

Session-based recommendation is gaining traction due to its broad potential, and one session-based recommendation model is MIND, which utilizes cross-encoding in a multi-layered structure to produce better results than traditional rank-models. However, MIND is prone to memory leaks, and its variation, MINDII, which uses data augmentation has not been as successful. Our proposed method addresses this limitation and provides data augmentation through self-supervised learning by randomly swapping item pairs in the session. Since AUC is not affected by labeling or switching targets, we incorporate switching into the training process. The resulting model outperforms MINDII and achieves par with state-of-the-art methods.

This research investigates subgroups of the unit groups in group rings for finite nilpotent groups of class two, which then yields constructions for self-orthogonal or complementary group codes and linear complementary codes (LCD codes) using these subgroups. By using a subgroup of a group ring element under a specific condition, we derive new families of group codes with promising parameters for practical applications.

We establish a stable realization for the cohomology of the group GL(n,R) using a specific set of invariant differential forms. These invariant forms serve as the stable source for the cohomology structure of GL(n,R) within the framework of p-adic stable homotopy theory. Additionally, we obtain a precise computation for the stable real cohomology of the group GL(n,R).

We've observed aux variables aux_var in recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and
found their location in the network is both accessible and predictive of performance.
Our analysis of empirical data reveals distinct patterns of performance for models
with and without aux variables. Models without aux variables display an even
distribution of performance, whereas those with aux variables excel when the
number of aux variables is increased. We developed theoretical models based on
energy functions and found they match the observed patterns in the data. These
findings suggest that Recurrent Neural Networks are prone to specific types of errors
and introduce a new framework for analyzing the testability of RNNs.

The non-Hermitian skin effect is a significant phenomenon that arises in open chains with non-Hermitian physics like topological insulators and is notable for its sensitivity to initial and boundary conditions. Understanding how the skin effect is influenced by real-world factors such as disorder and correlations is crucial. This work investigates the impact of unidirectional correlations in the extended Hatano-Nelson chain, finding that the skin area can increase with the number of unidirectional hops. Additionally, the intensity of the skin effect is only influenced by the difference between forward and backward hopping rates when only one type of correlation is present. However, when both types of correlation are involved, an additional dependency on their specific rates is observed. This was further verified through numerical simulations of the skin wavefunction.

This research presents a new method for creating DC-balanced quaternary Golay complementary array pairs of any given length. Our approach involves constructing such pairs using the parts from two specific quaternary Golay complementary double shift registers. By applying this method, we can produce DC-balanced quaternary Golay complementary array pairs of any desired odd or even length. Furthermore, we prove that certain lengths are restricted for these pairs, including feasible lengths of the form $3 \cdot (6k-1)$ and infeasible lengths of $2(3k-1)$. Examples are provided to demonstrate the construction of these pairs.

Recent LHC Run 2 data from the 13 TeV ATLAS and CMS runs have placed new constraints on the LHC, specifically the anomalous vector boson couplings to the Higgs boson. By analyzing the seven-vector model, which includes eight couplings, this research establishes limits on eight parameters. Luminous LHC data from 133 inverse femtobarns, spanning the 2016-2018 period, specifically addressed the decay of the Higgs boson to two photons, an event that spanned a mass range of 125 GeV, by considering the transverse mass. LHC findings also show the absence of the Higgs boson's decay to two Z bosons, an intermediate step in which the Higgs boson decays directly to two photons. LHC results confirm that the constraints on the anomalous Higgs boson couplings are in line with the predictions of the standard model, and the constraints are set at less than 10 percent for most coupling parameters, which is less than one-vote of its vacuum energy in the standard model.

Change detection in multi-temporal imagery is crucial for various remote sensing applications, but it presents a major challenge due to the vast amount of unlabeled imagery available. While current method comparisons focus on supervised approaches, there is a notable absence of analysis for unsupervised and deep learning-based change detection methods in the literature. This study aims to fill this gap by creating comprehensive benchmarks for both unsupervised and deep learning-based change detection approaches in visible and SAR imagery. The research finds that unsupervised change detection uses less labeled data than supervised methods while achieving comparable results, and in some cases, even outperforms them. Furthermore, a novel loss function is introduced for unsupervised semantic segmentation in change detection, enhancing overall performance. The study also explores the effectiveness of using pre-trained models for change detection tasks in visible and SAR images, with experimental results indicating the potential for pre-training to significantly improve the performance of change detection models in visible and SAR image datasets.

We establish that for any positive integer $n$, the maximum sum of squares of complementary sets to a subset of $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$ is limited to $O(n^{7/4} (\log n)^2)$. This achievement represents an enhancement from the prior complexity of $O(n^2 / (\log n)^{1/4})$.

We've developed an analytical method to examine how Heisenberg spin exchange interacts within a silicon crystal lattice doped with isolated spins. For heaveside coupling interaction, our method uses an expanded Green's function to derive the exact atomic position dependence of the interaction. It's our first thought that the ability to control and place interactions at this level of precision could greatly enhance the potential for quantum computation using Heisenberg coupling interaction for linking quantum bits.

Local search methods, a class of implicit implicit Monte Carlo algorithms, can be used to generate new states during the Markov chain process. A study is conducted to explore the application of combinatorial optimization benchmarks to improve implicit implicit Monte Carlo algorithms. A tool, libOPT, is developed to facilitate this research, which incorporates 53 benchmarks from various sources, including modified functions. Additionally, libOPT features three algorithms: Simulated Annealing, Iterative Improvement, and Iterative Fatiguing, which are extensively tested for efficiency. A comprehensive comparison of the benchmarks and three methods is conducted to evaluate their performance. Furthermore, libOPT allows for the customization of benchmarks through parameter adjustment, which serves as an effective way for researchers to contribute to the tool and explore new areas of research.

We have determined the transitivity degree for complete intersections in algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero, within the context of certain types of algebraic varieties known as projective varieties with hyperplane sections.

The paper delves into the description of total momentum within non-abelian quantum systems, drawing primarily on principles relevant to physicists engaged in this description language. It briefly touches upon key group theoretical aspects necessary to formulate total momentum within multi-particle quantum systems without resorting to extensive elaboration. The intended outcome is to facilitate physicists' understanding and application of these momentum descriptions without necessitating in-depth consultations by professional group theorists. The influential role and applications of Wigner's construction are central to this description, and multi-particle total momentum is defined through individual particle momenta without ambiguity. The study also emphasizes the significance and specific applications of induced representations in multi-particle quantum systems.

When a semiconductor absorbs two photons at the same time, an electron is released into the conduction band, leaving behind two holes. To model this process, an extended version of the drift-diffusion equations is used, which includes a non-linear system of partial differential equations. In many applications, it is assumed that the photons are evenly distributed, which allows for a space variable to be eliminated from the model. However, due to complex boundary interactions, we cannot apply a common approach to prove the existence of a solution. Instead, a new direct method is used to obtain a solution within a specific function space. Furthermore, a modified time-discretization approach is implemented to prove the convergence of approximate solutions to the full model.

Language models are increasingly being used in both N M-L and P M-l applications.
However, existing models often struggle with generalizing misogyny across different
domains, making it challenging to create effective, domain-agnostic systems for
detecting and preventing online harassment. This work addresses the limitation by
introducing a new dataset (MARBench) and an associated model, MARBench, which
improves the ability of online harassment detectors to recognize domain-specific
misogyny through a supervised transfer learning approach. Additionally, we
conducted experiments using MARBench to evaluate the performance of several
N M-L and P M-l models, revealing that incorporating a larger pre-trained model
through transfer learning yields state-of-the-art results in text classification
and binary classification on the dataset.

This research focuses on the solvability of a backward stochastic differential equation (BSDE) whose generator utilizes past values, incorporating a linear growth condition and a linear constraint on the solution's first component. It also involves a terminal payment that's affected by the past values of another process. To establish a unique solution, the research makes use of a novel transformation and an iteration approach. The findings are verified against a particular case that models a relevant quadratic reflection problem.

Reinforcement learning achieves exceptional performance in control systems, albeit through an extremely challenging process that often proves infeasible in real-world applications. By simplifying the planning problem into a Minkowski sum of the current state and possible transitions, we can generate a precomputed map that narrows down optimal options. Employing a Markov decision process within this framework and applying proximal policy optimization, we develop a learned policy to navigate future states, leveraging our precomputed map. By enforcing a minimum level of noise in our dynamics model, we significantly enhance the controller's resilience to mispredictions, while limiting the size of plausible transitions improves sample efficiency by a factor of ten, without sacrificing robustness. Additionally, we integrate a robust action pruning step to further reinforce our controllers. In comprehensive evaluations, where we extensively stress-tested the systems, our approach exhibited remarkable resilience to modeling inaccuracies, perturbations, and distributional shifts, while consistently matching or surpassing state-of-the-art controllers in standard learning tasks.

A proposed method for coded caching reduces file transfer latency during peak traffic by reducing the amount of data files must be transmitted from servers to users over the internet. The method divides files into smaller units, which correspond to vertices in a hypergraph, and stores subsets of these units across all files. By exploiting the structure of these subsets, a smaller amount of data is transmitted to each file. We introduce a mathematical framework that connects caching schemes with a specific type of hypergraph, known as resolvable covering arrays. This framework enables the efficient use of space in caching by utilizing commutative semirings. This approach yields new results for caching schemes based on Reed-Solomon and LFSR codes.

This study proposes a constructive and predicative Scott model for predicative dependent type theory with a cumulative hierarchy of types and a total approach. Our model incorporates a system for managing inductive families, which serves as a framework for interpreting universes. By adopting a specific arrangement of universes, we show that this model is capable of faithfully representing Scott's approach to language design. Furthermore, we develop a model for an interactive system with a Scott-based foundation, enabling the interpretation of higher-order dependent types within a predicative system. Ultimately, we establish a total functional programming paradigm through the use of a higher-order encoding system, effectively linking the Scott model to Scott's approach to language design.

A specific subset of the Weyl group's cosets is explored to express certain elements within a particular subset of the integers. It's proven that these specific integers are fundamental in describing the coefficients of a particular category of degenerate Eisenstein series associated with the Sp(2n,Z) group. Moreover, an important result is obtained, revealing that these degenerate Eisenstein series are orthogonal to each other. This finding enables the expansion of another Eisenstein series, specific to the Sp(2n,Z) group, into a series of other Eisenstein series, specific to the Sp(r,Z) (r>=2) groups. It's also discovered that this particular series features only positive coefficients.

Our key contribution is the integration of complex projective geometry with
motion planning to navigate through the spatial configurations of a multi-segment
robotic arm.  This approach leverages the spatial arrangement of a robotic arm's
segments by extending its vertices and edges to form a spatial configuration
map, effectively capturing the interconnectedness of these segments.  Building on
this framework, we develop a collision avoidance strategy for a robotic arm with
multiple segments, particularly focusing on the final segment, to avoid obstacles
while navigating its course.  This method's innovation lies in the use of complex
geometry to understand the robotic arm's configuration, which also facilitates
smooth course adjustments to evade obstacles.  In addition, we enhance the basic
strategy by taking into account both past and present positions of the target
object to anticipate and counter potential collisions proactively.  Finally, our
research includes the development of both simulated and real-world experiments to
validate the effectiveness of this collision avoidance technique.

To some extent, NLP to NLP has already been underway – by studying the
evolution of language from the past to the present. Our study, however, takes a
different approach by focusing on the variety of language used today. Why does
NLP to NLP strive for a more unified, simplified, and effective communication
system? Because our current methods of written and spoken communication are
already too complex. Let's imagine a scenario where we're trying to teach a
computer the meaning of the sentence "I love you." We've found that simply
translating it from another language isn't a reliable approach – there are too
many nuances and contexts to consider. Instead, we've tried to design a
more efficient system by leveraging the power of the English language. Our
approach involves using a simplified, standardized form of English that is
both written and spoken. This would make it much easier for a computer to
understand the sentence "I love you." Our method, in effect, is an attempt to
unify the English language – much like the Vulgate sought to unify the Bible.
However, we're not trying to rewrite English from the beginning – instead, we're
trying to establish a simpler, more standardized form of English that is
both written and spoken. This would make it much easier for a computer to
understand the sentence "I love you."

The sensitivity of the Ramsey interferometry technique to Bose-Einstein condensates is a well-documented phenomenon. Recently, a research team proposed a new method using nonlinear phase gates and found it could significantly improve the protocol. They introduced hadamard and controlled-z gates composed of controlled-phase and single-qubit phases, which can be realized using laser light or Feshbach scattering. The new method achieves a phase sensitivity increase of two times, while the original protocol offers a one-fold improvement. We now extend this research by proposing a quantum key distribution protocol that leverages the enhanced performance of nonlinear hadamard gates. The protocol utilizes the Fock states of light as an encoding basis, which can be manipulated using a cavity QED system and detected using technology based on photon-number resolving detectors. The system allows for a maximum security rate of 0.17 bits per signal, which translates to one bit per signal at short distances.

This work relates to a novel interpolation problem in complex analysis. Given $q$ mappings, $F_1, \dots, F_q$, from a complex projective space to another, and considering their intersections with $n$ hypersurfaces and the presence of $l$ movable branches, under the condition that their combined dimensions exceed a calculated value based on $q$, $n$, $l$, and the degree of the hypersurfaces, we prove that these mappings must be constant. The theorem we have developed generalizes several existing non-defectivity theorems.

This paper presents an innovative approach that integrates signature-based Gröbner basis algorithms into the computation of polynomial system solutions. By leveraging this method, we efficiently incorporate properties of the Groebner basis into the solution calculation process. The results are supported by numerical experiments, which demonstrate improvements over the conventional Groebner basis approach and Homomorphic Backsubstitution. Furthermore, the proposed method is adaptable to other methods for solving polynomial systems, allowing it to benefit from their inherent advantages.

A study of direct photons from 0.1-2 GeV/c in 40-62 GeV $\\rm Cu+Cu$ collisions at RHIC has been conducted at star anisotropy runs, measuring a rapidity density, 100$\\rm{m/c}$, of 40-47% of the density from 200 GeV $\\rm Au+Au$ collisions. The shape of the rapidity distribution follows a Gaussian and the yield follows a power law, $P_T^{-n}$, of 5.16$\\rm{Cu}\\rm{+Cu}$, slightly lower than the 5.77 from 200 GeV $\\rm Au+Au$ studies. The findings show that a lower photon $T_n$ and a higher $n_{q}$ of 1.5 for $\\rm Cu^+$ collisions compared to 1.2 for 200 GeV $\\rm Au+Au$ collisions indicates a quicker increase of photon yield at low $T_n$ for $\\rm Cu+Cu$ collisions. The results also reveal a 30-40% higher average number of initial nucleon-nucleon interactions per event at low $T_n$ for $\\rm Cu+Cu$ collisions. The study found a difference in the average number of interactions between mid-central events and minimum head-on events. In the former

The function exco_2(n,H) represents the maximum number of edges a 4-uniform n-vertex hypergraph can have without containing H as a subgraph, where H is K_4 without one of its edges. Research demonstrates that exco_2(n,H) exhibits quadratic growth, its values are bounded both above and below by a constant for certain choices of H, and its asymptotic behavior changes depending on H when those other edges are included.

Our primary goal is to enhance the rendering of curved or rounded line joins in vector graphics, particularly those in GIS data, by addressing the problem of excessive pixel output in standard rendering methods. The existing approach leads to incorrect and inefficient pixel output, which in turn causes significant performance issues when rendering large datasets. We have developed an algorithm that optimizes pixel output and yields a time complexity of O(n), enabling the accurate and efficient rendering of fan-shaped line joins of any size. This proposal further improves the size and performance of rendered curved or rounded line joins in vector graphics, especially within GIS data. Its effects extend to the improvement of rendering other geometric shapes, such as curved arc joins and rounded or round joins, ultimately leading to faster rendering and better overall performance.

This paper develops a quasi-interpolation formula based on the novel radius-based width function, a tool that connects a function's condition number to its Cauchy data on spheres. We change the function's representation to preserve positivity, convexity, and monotonicity in the method. Additionally, we present an alternative quasi-interpolation formula using the function's modified negative radius-based width. This formula maintains properties like smoothness, convexity, and monotonicity while reducing the method's accuracy order by one.

Recent findings from the HAWC Observatory and HESS Observatory suggest the presence of a TeV gamma-ray excess in the galactic center, potentially attributed to pulsar populations with pulsar wind nebulae and pulsar wind terminal shocks. Analysis of pulsar halos indicates they can be significantly observed in the MeV band, leading to claims of explaining the cosmic positron excess. However, our research demonstrates that the MeV emission from these halos is heavily absorbed by the interstellar medium and produces negligible Borexino-compatible signals. Furthermore, our measurements of pulsar age and nebula age indicate a substantial population of pulsars without associated nebulae and yield negligible total MeV flux and age-weighted MeV flux. Consequently, pulsar halos are unlikely to be the primary source of the observed gamma-ray and positron excesses.

This research paper investigates methods to enhance the efficiency of Affective Neural Networks in classifying images, focusing on the use of Data Augmentation and Super Pixel Delimiting Masks. To increase the training dataset and diversity, we employ a combination of traditional image manipulation techniques and a novel method based on organ-specific masks. These masks aid in concentrating the network's learning on key image features and symmetrical class representation. We also investigate the efficacy of these methods when used individually and in conjunction with other image manipulation techniques, such as geometric augmentations and image augmentation. Our experiments were conducted on the FER2013 and AFK datasets, and the results indicate that using organ-specific masks in isolation outperforms data augmentation alone and enhances performance when combined with other image manipulation techniques.

This work investigates climate change as a prominent scientific issue, exploring its evolution into a political issue and an economic one. Initially, a content analysis was conducted on over 350 articles from two established indexes, which showed that the average level of interest from policymakers in addressing climate change was around 36%, while that of featured economics was 44% and general interest science journals and magazines 53%. Furthermore, a study found that the average interest from policymakers in addressing climate change had increased over time, with a similar increase seen for featured economics but a similar decrease seen for general interest science journals and magazines. This work proposes that this discrepancy occurs because economists and scientists are often interested in addressing climate change for their own purposes, while policymakers are often interested in other topics as well. Consequently, an alternative method of content analysis was developed that could better reflect the real impact of these discussions, which was then applied to that analysis.

Recent breakthroughs in soft robotics have generated significant interest but also presented complex challenges, primarily linked to the physical properties of rubber. The (Koopman) operator theory is a data-driven approach that has been effectively applied to various nonlinear control problems, but current methods typically collect data first and then use it to estimate the operator. This paper takes a different approach by leveraging the structured nature of soft systems, where actuation locations and patterns are well understood, to directly model the operator without the need for extensive data collection. The method focuses on understanding the inverse of the system's evolution, highlighting regions of interest and associating them with input actions to design an efficient observation-based action mapping. The efficiency of the approach is further improved by restricting its application to relevant system observations, allowing for immediate use of the derived action mapping as a observer in state-estimation-based controllers. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated through successful implementations on various types of soft systems, including inflatable actuators, worm-like fibers with controlled flexion, and rubber that changes shape through electrical stimulation.

We present a simplified approach for the Natural Gradient Descent method, designed for full rank approximations in both online and online batch settings. This approach integrates the Diagonal-Kernel Recursive Samelskii Algorithm 3 with the Stochastic Fisher Matrix Estimator to develop an efficient natural gradient method. We provide theoretical justifications, demonstrating that the proposed method offers significant advantages in convergence speed and computational efficiency compared to standard gradient descent methods. Our results indicate that the adaptive version of this approach achieves a convergence rate of $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ with an online algorithm and a convergence rate of $O(\sqrt{\log T}/T)$ with an online batch algorithm, while maintaining an average computational complexity of $O(\lceil \sqrt{\tau} + \tau \rceil)$ and $O(\lceil \sqrt{\tau} \rceil)$ respectively at each iteration. The online batch method, in particular, displays a logarithmic dependence on sample size, showcasing its high sample efficiency. We validate the efficacy of this approach through numerical experiments on various classification and regression tasks, demonstrating improved performance compared to standard gradient descent methods.

Recent findings from the Rubin Observatory's LSST have identified numerous features in imaging and spectroscopy of high-redshift Active Galactic Nuclei (AGNs). A thorough examination of the spectral and multi-band photometric spectrum (MPSPs) of 342 local AGNs is presented, each featuring distinct spectral features. A comprehensive analysis is provided for each feature to facilitate identification of features in upcoming high-z AGN datasets. A machine learning model is used to identify features from MPSPs, and the study finds that photometric features show a greater sensitivity to the size of the black hole, while the sensitivity to the ionization parameter varies with the inclusion of spectroscopic features. Furthermore, it is shown that features can be interpreted using simple radiative transfer models without invoking complex broad-line region geometries. Lastly, it is noted that features can be identified even in low signal-to-noise ratio spectra with significant uncertainty. These findings will be crucial in interpreting high-abundance AGN datasets.

The time of patient survival is a critical indicator used to assess the effectiveness of medical treatments. However, accurately predicting survival time has long been a difficult task for medical researchers. A recent study proposed Lite-ProSENet, a neural network model designed to improve patient survival time predictions by analyzing medical images and electronic health records. This new model outperformed existing methods in three benchmark datasets for lung cancer, ovarian cancer, and prostate cancer, with performance comparisons even to more complex models. Notably, Lite-ProSENet was successfully deployed on Google Cloud Healthcare API, marking it as one of the first open-source models to be released in that platform.
